rv.q: It all makes for an explosion of a show that feels surprisingly, joyously, fresh, a quarter of a century on.
East is East is an eruption of a show that forces us to consider it.
Happily, the second and longer half ups the ante...
Khan knows the right notes to hit to ensure it still works as well today, while also giving the production enough of its own flavour to make it worth revisiting.

cn.t: Ayub Khan Din's autobiographical comedy-drama about a mixed-race British Pakistani family in 1970s Salford resonates powerfully 25 years later, with critics praising its engaging portrayal of culture clash and identity struggles.
